paras: The whitecapping threat at Puncheon Run was an episode in December 1903 near Dover, Delaware, in which local citizens threatened to whitecap a white woman, Bertie Fleming, and a Black man named Smith who were living together. Rather than act against those making the threats, the sheriff and three officers arrested the couple on December 22 as "suspicious characters."

Fleming was described as a white woman of 20 and Smith as "a negro" of 45, and the two shared a house at Puncheon Run, near Dover. According to a Dover special to the Wilmington Evening Journal, there had been "threats of whitecapping the couple," though the report does not say who made them or when.

On the morning of December 22, 1903, Sheriff Melvin, Constable Williams and Policemen Killen and Russell surrounded the house and arrested both occupants. The correspondent wrote that the authorities "took time by the forelock" in making the arrest before the threats were carried out. No violence against the couple is reported.

The pair were to appear the next day before Magistrate Wood, where officers expected to charge them with unspecified "other crimes." No report of the hearing, of any charge, or of action against those who made the threats appears in the coverage.

The only known report ran on the front page of the Wilmington Evening Journal on December 22 under the headline "White Girl Living with Negro near Dover." Its deck, "Citizens Threatened Violence and Authorities Arrested the Couple," presented the arrest of the threatened pair as a sensible precaution, and the story made the couple's household rather than the threats its subject. No coverage in the Black press or in other white papers has been found.

accounts.gist: Citizens threatened to whitecap a white woman and a Black man living together; officers surrounded the house and arrested the pair as suspicious characters before any violence.
